utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The more observant of you will notice that there are not three. We anticipate that if we sit tomorrow Judge Van Den Wyngaert will be able to sit with us. We will continue sitting as two. Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, one brief matter. I think there must be a flu flying around The Hague, because one of our lawyers on the case is also sick, which really relates to the application I have today. I believe Mr. Moore raised the issue of presenting some of the Rule 92 evidence this week before the Easter break. Ms. Tuma will be dealing with that, but unfortunately this week as well she's been unwell. So we would ask that that be put forward to after the Easter break. And the next witness that was planned was a military witness who I've been advised, the Prosecution believe would take at least three days to testify. And in light of that, the Prosecution is not really in a position to present a witness today before -- after this witness, and before the Easter break starts. And, in part, the gap in time, the day and a half that perhaps will be made available or free has been due to the fact that the Prosecution slightly miscalculated how quickly the cross-examinations of the re-called witnesses last week was going to proceed. So if I could just advise the Court of that situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, effectively you're saying that we will conclude today, assuming this witness's evidence finished today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any objection to that from counsel? Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to all. Thank you, Your Honours. No objection whatsoever. It does seem, however, that we have little time, as we are, and it is on behalf of all three Defence teams that I would like to raise some issues, which I think it is important to have ruled on before we head for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, could that be done now, or after the witness has finished his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we could deal with these issues once we have finished with the witness. I think we shall be requiring no more than five minutes after the witness leaves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can't deny Mr. Lukic and Mr. Borovic their full measure. Very well. We will now have the witness in and move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vasic, you've waited patiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I did point out on behalf of all three Defence teams that I would like to raise two issues that strike me as important. This is in relation to the submission we received from our learned friends on the 10th of April this year, although we expected to arrive a lot earlier such as announced by my learned friend, Mr. Moore. The motion is marked as confidential. Maybe, just maybe that might require us to go into private session, Your Honour, so that we can raise some issues in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are your submissions about it ones that give rise to confidential matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the issues doesn't, in actual fact. I may as well raise that issue right away. It's in relation to our reply, Your Honours. I would like to present our position and ask for the Trial Chamber's understanding in relation to this particular situation. The other issue, I think, is directly related to the fact that the submission was marked as confidential, and I think that we might be better off doing that in private session. I might raise the first matter now, for all it's worth. After three months of trial, we are now facing a position of being given a short break, something to do with the religious festivities approaching. However, I do have to say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to change that and not have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that was what I was going to ask for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so tread carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. But we've covered that ground before, and this is our joint position. We shall be taking advantage of only a very small portion of this recess or break for the purpose of celebrating these festivities. We shall be using the best part of the time to get in touch with our own investigators and to give them further instructions to get on verifying a number of facts that we've heard from a variety of witnesses here over the last couple of weeks. Furthermore, we shall be meeting our Defence experts, especially in view of the witnesses coming right after the break, witnesses who are members of military units. Therefore, Your Honours, the Defence would like to ask the following: The Defence would like to ask to be granted more time for our reply to this motion. The motion is of a very serious nature, and the Defence will have to address a number of issues and address all the documents that have been used in these proceedings, both at the pre-trial stage and during the actual trial. We shall certainly be needing a little more time in order to be able to do that. So under its authority under Rule 127, may the Trial Chamber please bear all these things in mind, as well as the additional factor, which is that we have to get translations for our clients. This is very important and has a bearing on whatever their responsibility might be under the indictment. This applies to all three Defence teams, and given the circumstances, the 28th of April might be a fitting extension. That is the end of the week of our return. If Your Honours believe that this is too long, can we at least have the general 14-day extension that is granted under Rule 126 bis? And if this could then be dealt with on the 25th of April in the morning, so the Defence teams are given sufficient time to take care of business back in Belgrade and so that we are able to file our reply in good time. So much for the first issue that I was about to raise, Your Honours. I would like now to move on to my second issue. For my second issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is well aware that there are many demands on time on counsel and that they also put big pressures on family and other commitments. The Chamber, in its time, has had to live that way itself, as counsel. We are aware of the problems. But you will also appreciate that from the point of view of the accused, the sooner this trial is finished, the better. Therefore, we have to expect of counsel that their work will be done expeditiously. We, therefore, tend to sit five days a week, week after week so that this case can finish as soon as possible. Now, if there is a genuine need for adjournment, either for some significant personal reason, or if the demands of a particular part of the work justify it, you can be sure that it will be considered and granted, if justified, but, otherwise, we need to maintain a hard-working pace. You want further time now, it's important, you say. It happens to coincide with the first break that we have agreed to. For that reason, we are prepared to extend time until the 28th of April for your response. It does mean that we will not be able to work on it and give a decision immediately on your return. We would point out, as you have mentioned in some of the things that you will be doing during the break, that this trial will continue to move with as much expedition as possible, so that at the end of the Prosecution case, if there is to be a motion under Rule 98 bis, under the terms of the new rule as amended, it will need to happen then, not after a delay for you to think about it. And we would also point out that it is the Chamber's intention to proceed with a minimum of delay to the Defence evidence, if each of you is to call evidence, or if any of you are to call evidence. Which means that the longest break that you can hope for, after any 98 bis submission, is in the order of two weeks or perhaps three. Not months. So if there is clear in everybody's mind, when you're thinking whether you can afford another weekend off, bear this in mind. And you will realise, in the end, the purpose is so that the trial can conclude. Everybody, especially the accused, will know the outcome. They have had a long time wanting to know what the outcome of these allegations are, and it's important that this Chamber and this Tribunal does what it can to ensure that that waiting for themselves and their family and all others who are interested is kept to the shortest possible time. It appears that there is nothing further that is to be raised before we break for the two celebrations of the Easter festival. Is that correct? May we wish all of you a happy Easter and a time, I hope, with your families. We will resume on the Tuesday after the Orthodox Easter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, there is one brief matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: After that lovely speech. You've spoiled it all, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, the case manager in this case, Sandra D'Angelo is leaving the case, and Mr. Andres Vatter will be the new case manager. She is going to the Rwanda Tribunal, and we appreciate -- we have appreciated her assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think all of us would join in that and we wish her well. Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would just like to wish everyone a very happy Easter on behalf of the Defence teams. And most of all I would like to thank Ms. D'Angelo for her kind and successful cooperation with all our teams. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of April, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.21 p.m.,
